decisions.decision: Read the whole arrangement once per list load and hand the resolved lugger to the card through the availability record
decisions.why: Cell resolution is static and synchronous, and the card already reads values it was handed; one read per load beats one per card
decisions.rejected: Making cell resolution asynchronous and injecting the service into the card path

decisions.decision: Store the dump-point role on the scrap-type assignment row and keep status on the lugger
decisions.why: A lugger can take two scrap types, so one status cannot encode a per-type role, and FR-016 forbids deriving the role from order alone
decisions.rejected: Deriving the dump point as the first usable lugger in order

decisions.decision: Delete a removed lugger and keep its name as text in the change row
decisions.why: FR-003 requires a removed name to be re-creatable, and MySQL 5.7 has no partial unique index to let a retired row keep the name
decisions.rejected: A soft is_active flag, which collides with the unique name on re-creation

decisions.decision: One idempotent seed that inserts the defaults only when the lugger table is empty
decisions.why: The defaults are a starting arrangement, so a re-run must not duplicate them or undo a lead rename, and the same artifact lands on an installed store
decisions.rejected: A truncating base seed plus a separate migration seed

decisions.decision: Match scrap types on case and surrounding spaces only
decisions.why: FR-009 says exactly that, and the setup list spells 5052 aluminum while the spec pins 5052 Aluminum
decisions.rejected: Collapsing inner whitespace, which would let a genuinely different spelling match

decisions.decision: Every mutating procedure writes its own arrangement-change rows in its own transaction
decisions.why: The audit and the notice cannot drift apart, and a write that records nothing cannot be authored
decisions.rejected: A shared audit procedure called by the application, which one call site can forget

decisions.decision: Poll the change table on the existing minute tick with a per-session watermark set when the list opens
decisions.why: FR-037 is a statement about where the client starts, which a watermark gives exactly, and no dismissal table is then needed
decisions.rejected: A per-user read cursor in the store, which replays changes made while the person was away

decisions.decision: Reordering or assigning re-derives the dump point to the first usable lugger in the new order
decisions.why: FR-006 says the order is the order the system tries, so an order where the second lugger held the role would make the two disagree
decisions.rejected: Leaving the role where it was after a reorder

decisions.decision: The arrangement writes open the provider connection in LuggerArrangementService and read affected_rows from the procedure's result set, instead of going through the retrying IMySqlHelperServer.
decisions.why: A transaction-wrapped CALL answers the COMMIT's count (0), and the helper retries and folds a SIGNAL into its neutral result, so a refusal would read as a change that landed and a retry could duplicate a write. PermissionAdministrationService and UserManagementRepository already use this shape for the same reason.
decisions.rejected: A second affected-row column on the non-query seam, or client-side-only validation with the store's refusal message lost.

decisions.decision: The Setup scrap picker composes its list as ScrapDecisionRules' two decision words plus ScrapTypeCatalog.All, rather than the catalogue holding those two words.
decisions.why: The catalogue is the shipped scrap types and nothing else (FR-010); the two words decide whether there is scrap and may never be assigned to a lugger, while the picker must still offer them, so the composition belongs where the picker is built.
decisions.rejected: Putting 'Scrap Type Required' and 'No Scrap' in the catalogue and filtering them out in the editor.

decisions.decision: RoleRestrictionInventoryTests (T007) and PermissionBaselineParityTests (T006) were amended alongside the tasks that invalidated them.
decisions.why: Both pin the declaration's Settings keys and the Material Handler Lead baseline, so the new key broke them and no task in tasks.md owned either file.
decisions.rejected: Leaving them red until an unlisted later task, or weakening their coverage assertions.

decisions.decision: Adding a lugger at an occupied display position shifts every row at or after it up by one, inside the same transaction.
decisions.why: The procedure convention is a distinct and contiguous display order, and refusing an occupied position would make the editor depend on numbering the lead cannot see.
decisions.rejected: A unique key on display_position, which would reject the intermediate state mid-shift.

decisions.decision: AllSeeds.sql was resynced with seed_permission_role_baselines/create.sql in this change.
decisions.why: Installing the aggregates into a scratch store showed the nine new permission rows were in the artifact only; AllSeeds.sql is what the installer runs, so a fresh store would never have received them. DatabaseAggregateRegistrationTests cannot see this because it matches the first line only.
decisions.rejected: Leaving the aggregate stale because its artifact-registration gate passes.

decisions.decision: Reorder by dragging a card, written through sp_waitlist_lugger_locations_position_set, and recorded without a handler notice
decisions.why: The lead is arranging their own screen, so the change is an edit worth recording (FR-032) but sends no handler anywhere differently, and FR-033 does not list it.
decisions.rejected: Stepping a lugger one place with Move up and Move down, which needed two buttons, a position readout and a write per step.

decisions.decision: Report a failed write and a failed read as two different things
decisions.why: The store still answers the read, so the cards on screen are still the stores own; clearing them reports a write fault as a read fault and takes away the list the reader would use to see nothing changed.
decisions.rejected: Reusing the unavailable state for both, which is what emptied the page after the first failed edit.

plan.summary: Planned a live lugger-arrangement read for the scrap card, a permissioned settings editor with a stored transition engine, and an in-app change notice.
plan.key_finding: The card slot and its declaration already exist; the whole feature is a configuration read plus one resolver arm, not a card or seed change.

tasks.summary: 71 tasks in 7 phases: 1 setup, 35 foundational (3 tables, 11 procedures, 3 aggregates, seed, permission, service), 8 card, 3 transition proofs, 8 editor, 9 notice, 7 polish.

specify.summary: Scrap Lugger Location shipped: three tables and eleven procedures behind one arrangement seam, the pickup-scrap card resolving its lugger from configuration with the In development placeholder retired, a permissioned Settings arrangement page, and an in-application change notice.

implement.summary: Implemented 013 end to end, then revised the Settings surface the owner asked for: lugger cards with their own Edit and Rename, modal editor and name dialogs, a scrap-type ComboBox, a filtered Make dump point, and drag-to-reorder replacing the move buttons.
implement.key_finding: Reading the arrangement fell back to the local store and writing did not, so every edit timed out on a workstation off the plant network and the page reported it as unreadable.
implement.risks: The cards, dialogs and drag are proven by markup and view-model tests only; no run against a store happened on this machine, and the twelve database objects are deployed locally but not on the plant host.

approach: A new configuration capability in mtm_waitlist holds seven seeded luggers, each scrap type ordered list of luggers, and a dump-point role stored on the assignment row, with every transition performed inside the stored procedure that makes the edit. The scrap card reads the whole arrangement once per list load, resolves the requesting jobs scrap type without regard to case or surrounding spaces, and draws the dump point name, or the first lugger plus its status when none can receive. A permissioned Settings page maintains the arrangement, and the waitlist polls the recorded changes on its existing minute tick so each handler sees each change once inside the application.

FR-001.title: Maintain a managed set of named luggers, each with a name, a status and a position in the display order

FR-002.title: A fresh installation ships the seven named luggers

FR-003.title: Every lugger is renameable, removable and re-creatable; none is fixed

FR-004.title: A lugger name is unique across the set, compared without regard to case

FR-005.title: Removing a lugger removes its assignments and leaves none pointing at it

FR-006.title: A scrap type names an ordered set of luggers, and the order is the order tried

FR-007.title: A lugger may take several scrap types and a scrap type may name several luggers

FR-008.title: A fresh installation ships the seven pinned assignments

FR-009.title: A job's scrap type matches its assignment ignoring letter case and surrounding spaces only

FR-010.title: Scrap Type Required and No Scrap are never assignable and never produce a lugger

FR-011.title: The editor offers the recognised scrap types and accepts one that is not among them

FR-012.title: A lugger carries exactly one status: Available, Backup, Full, or Do Not Use with a reason

FR-013.title: Exactly one lugger holds the dump point per scrap type whenever one can receive material

FR-014.title: The system performs the status transitions; a lead does not reconcile by hand

FR-015.title: Blocking the dump point promotes the next lugger in that scrap type's order

FR-016.title: An emptied lugger returns to Backup and does not reclaim the dump point

FR-017.title: A blocked lugger is never ordered above the dump point

FR-018.title: A lead may promote a chosen lugger, and the previous dump point returns to Backup

FR-019.title: Do Not Use requires a reason that a handler can read

FR-020.title: A status change leaves every affected scrap type complete

FR-021.title: A lugger's status applies to every scrap type assigned to it

FR-022.title: The Lugger Location cell shows the name of the lugger holding the dump point

FR-023.title: The value is read when the card is drawn, not stored on the request

FR-024.title: When no lugger can receive, the cell names the first lugger with its status

FR-025.title: No real scrap decision draws no lugger cell and is not recorded as a failure

FR-026.title: An unassigned scrap type draws no cell and records the gap

FR-027.title: The cell's label stays Lugger Location and the card layout does not change

FR-028.title: A permission of its own governs the arrangement, held by Material Handler Lead and above

FR-029.title: A person without the permission cannot open the arrangement by any route

FR-030.title: The arrangement is reachable from settings as a summary with an editor behind an explicit action

FR-031.title: The editor shows, for each scrap type, which lugger holds the dump point

FR-032.title: Every change to the arrangement records who made it and when

FR-033.title: Handlers using the application are told inside the application what changed

FR-034.title: The notice is in-application; no operating-system notification is used

FR-035.title: A notice names what changed, naming the lugger, the scrap type and both values

FR-036.title: Each person sees a notice once, and dismissing it does not let it return

FR-037.title: A change made while the person was not using the application is not replayed

FR-038.title: A person without the handle permission is not interrupted by the notice

FR-039.title: The In development placeholder is retired completely

concerns.note: The Settings entry, the arrangement page and the notice strip are WinUI surfaces; no running application or XamlMcp agent was available, so what is proven is that every x:Bind path compiles and the view-model and service layers behave under test. The visible round trip (entry appears for a lead, two bars, closing one leaves the other) was not exercised.
SC-004 and SC-005 are met at the view-model and service level only; the live two-session notice scenario and the in-app rename/remove/add/reassign round trip need a running app against the store.

The arrangement is read once per availability resolution, which the list caches per work centre, so a load costs one arrangement read per distinct work centre rather than literally one. A strictly single read per load needs a load-scoped signal on IRequestJobPartAvailabilityProvider, which no task owned.

validate-sql-naming.ps1 exits 1 on 13 pre-existing findings (the mock population file names, two restore scripts, and the legacy require_password_change / requires_answer columns). This feature contributes zero findings after the temp column was renamed is_previous_dump_point.

validate-database-schema.ps1 run against the local mtm_waitlist reports the 14 objects this feature adds as missing, because installing them is outside this run's read-only mandate. Validation ran with exit 0 against a scratch store installed from the aggregates in order (AllTables, AllFunct, AllViews, AllSPs, AllSeeds).

Two task descriptions count differently from the shipped data: T009 says the catalogue holds 'seven shipped types' where the setup list carries six distinct real spellings, and T021 says the seeded arrangement returns eleven rows where seven luggers with seven pairings return seven. The code follows the contract tables.

This change resolved no living-spec capability, so nothing was loaded before it and nothing was folded after it. Either the areas it touched belong to no capability yet, or a capability claims them and no requirement describes them — `living-validate` names which.

Root cause of the arrangement reporting itself unreadable after any edit on this workstation: LuggerArrangementService opened the raw configured connection string for writes, so with the plant host unreachable every write waited out Connect Timeout, while the read path fell back through MySqlHostFallback. Writes now resolve through LuggerWriteConnection with the same fallback, pinned to mtm_waitlist.

A write that fails is no longer reported as the unavailable state: the page keeps the cards the store answered and says the change was not saved (WriteFailedText); a missing procedure or table reports StoreOutOfDateText rather than inviting a retry that cannot work.

The local mtm_waitlist was missing sp_waitlist_lugger_locations_position_set, so the first drag hit a procedure that did not exist. The artifact was applied to the store and exercised there on a no-op move; any other store, including the plant host, still needs all twelve objects deployed.
The WinUI surfaces have still not been seen running against a store from this machine: the cards, both dialogs and the drag are proven by markup and view-model tests, not by a run.

New procedure sp_waitlist_lugger_locations_position_set and change kind lugger_reordered: the order is renumbered contiguously in one transaction and the reorder is recorded but deliberately not announced.
Make dump point is drawn only when the chosen scrap type is assigned to that lugger, another lugger is assigned as its backup, and this one is not already the dump point (CanPromote).

Card action words are bound from the row (LuggerArrangementRow.EditActionText and RenameActionText), not from the page: a GridView item template has its own name scope, so the ElementName binding to the page resolved to nothing and both buttons drew empty.

The cards are three across and the cell width is measured from the grid on load and on resize, so the columns span the panel; the cards margin opens the gutter inside its cell, so the width is a third of the grid rather than a third less the gutter.

Scrap card (spec 012 surface, no 013 artifact changed): Lugger Location is pinned to the second panel slot beside Scrap Type by WaitlistCardCellRules.OrderForPanel, so the pair reads the same whatever order a declaration carries.
